Subject: Next steps — model compatibility & callable acceptance tests (Acme Analytics)

Hi Sara / Tim,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier — appreciate the clear signals on success criteria. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the runbook for the trial: 

Recap (call highlights)
- Primary goal: reliably extract structured billing attributes from supplier invoices and surface normalized fields into Acme's ingestion pipeline with <= 150ms P50 on the request path for the production tier.
- Non-functional: JSON schema strictness (fields required, types), deterministic field mapping for auditability, and retries with idempotency for downstream processors.
- Data sensitivity: PII redaction and SOC2 evidence were mentioned; we'll include required artifacts.

Initial model compatibility recommendations (engineer-first):
- redwood-13b-q8 (low-latency candidate): good balance of cost/latency for interactive endpoints.
- redwood-70b-ptq (high-fidelity candidate): use for batch validation where quality matters more than absolute latency.
- redwood-13b-quant (edge quantized candidate): for strict throughput targets when batching heavily.

What we'll provide by the end of next week
1) Callable acceptance test plan (instrumented harness + pass/fail criteria). See attached stub: acme-requirements.pdf.
2) Prompt sets and seed dataset (sanitized) for reproducibility (Drive folder link below).
3) Sample JSON schema validator configuration and suggested retry semantics.
4) Mini-benchmark (latency/throughput) against the three recommended model flavors.

Proposed next steps / asks
- Can you share a short sample (10–20) of representative invoice JSON payloads (sanitized)? Prefer CSV or newline-delimited JSON.
- Confirm whether the schema is strict (fail on missing required fields) or best-effort (emit nulls).
- Align on canary size: we propose starting with 1% of production traffic for 24 hours, then ramp.

Scheduling
- I'll set up a 90-min runbook session with Engineering (Aditya) and Product (Priyom) next Tue to walk the callable tests and run a 1-hour smoke run. Please share availability.

Attachments: acme-requirements.pdf (overview)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-model-playbooks-example
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2027-0411

Quick note on observability: we'll include per-request schema validation traces and token-level latency breakdowns so you can tie regressions to model/config changes.

-Jordan

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Schema behavior: we need strict enforcement for downstream compliance, so the callable should fail fast (return a 4xx with structured error) when required fields are missing. That said, we want a configuration toggle for best-effort during canary.
- Retry semantics: our pipeline retries on 5xx and network timeouts, but not on application-level 4xx. We need idempotency tokens surfaced so retries don't create duplicate records.
- Auditability: we require immutable request/response logs for the canary period (30 days retention) plus an exportable CSV for validation.
- SOC2 docs: please attach SOC2 Type II attestation and the list of subservice organizations; procurement will need them for the vendor security checklist.

I've attached the current schema (acme-schema-v1.json) and a small sample set (10 invoices). We'll sanitize more if necessary.

Two quick asks: can you confirm which model will be the default behind the API for the canary, and whether we can pin a model revision (we need a stable artifact for audits)?

Thanks — Sara

Hi Sara — great, thanks for the schema and sample set. Quick answers then a proposed plan and the attached acceptance checklist (callable-test-plan.md).

Defaults & pinning
- Default model for the canary: redwood-13b-q8 (we recommend for latency-balanced canary). We will pin to a specific model revision sha (example: redwood-13b-q8@rev-20270408) for the canary run; that artifact will be recorded in the audit log.

Schema enforcement & error model
- We'll provide two runtime modes behind a single route: strict (default for canary) and lenient (toggle for ramp). Strict mode returns a 422 with structured error payload when required fields are missing. Lenient returns nulls and inserts a validation warning key for downstream processors.
- Logging: request id + model revision + validation result will be recorded; exportable as CSV. Retention: 30 days in the console (we can coordinate longer via dedicated retention add-on).

Callable acceptance test plan (high level) — attached more detail in callable-test-plan.md
- Functional checks: schema conformance across 200 seeded payloads, type checks, required-field enforcement.
- Stochastic checks: run 1,000 randomized seeds against the pinned model to measure schema violation rate and top-1 field mismatch rate.
- Tool/function calling tests: validate that functions are invoked only when the model returns a function call compliant with the ECD (expected callable descriptor). We'll fuzz for malformed callables and assert graceful failure modes.
- Retry/idempotency: test harness will replay failed requests with idempotency tokens and assert single-write semantics against a mocked downstream.
- Performance: target P50 <= 150ms for the route in strict mode, P95 <= 300ms. We'll record cold-starts and KV-cache hit ratios.

Engineering notes for your team (high level)
- Prompt sets: we'll check both extraction-first and example-driven prompts to see which yields lower schema violation.
- JSON validation: recommend AJV (with strict mode) and a schema contract test that runs in CI.
- Function calling semantics: design callables to be atomic (single function per intent) and require an explicit "confirmed" flag before side-effecting operations.

Next steps
1) We will upload the callable-test-plan.md and a mini-benchmark snapshot to the Drive folder by EOD today.
2) Please confirm a 90-min runbook slot Tue 2027-04-13 10:00–11:30 PT (or propose alternative).
3) Share a sanitized batch (50–100) of invoices for the stochastic checks.

Attachments: callable-test-plan.md (detailed acceptance checklist)

Cc: Aditya & Priyom — if you have technical addenda I should call out before the runbook, drop them below.

Thanks,

Sara / Jordan — a few technical points to set expectations before the runbook: 

1) Quantization and quality tradeoffs
- redwood-13b-q8: reliable for schema extraction and substantially lower latency; expect a small uptick in ambiguous entity boundaries versus the 70B PTQ model. We'll quantify that in the stochastic checks.
- redwood-70b-ptq: better at edge-case disambiguation (non-standard invoice layouts) but ~2–3x token-cost increase. Use for nightly batch reconciliation.

2) KV cache & function calling interactions
- When the callable route uses a KV cache for prefix tokens, ensure cache keys include the model revision + schema version + idempotency token to avoid accidental cache hits causing stale callables.
- We will instrument the runtime to emit a "callable_validation" trace when a function call is returned so you can filter for regressions.

3) Retry semantics & idempotency
- Best practice: clients should attach an idempotency token (UUID) per logical attempt; the callable should use that token to dedupe downstream writes.
- Retries should be safe for network errors/5xx. For 4xx validation errors we should not retry automatically.

4) Canary sizing & thresholds
- Canary start: 1% traffic for 24h. Automatic abort if schema-violation-rate > 1% or field-mismatch-rate increases by > 25% relative to baseline.
- Observability hooks: per-field failure counts, prompt-variant breakdown, model-revision tag.

5) Deliverables for the runbook
- Benchmarks: bench-results-20270410.csv (attached) containing latency profiles and token-cost simulations.
- Example CI contract test: we will provide a GitHub Actions snippet that runs the AJV schema check against any model output during PRs.

We'll upload the artifacts to the Drive folder and attach the SOC2 Type II certificate for procurement as a secure link during the contract phase. 

Let me know if you want a short pre-runbook sync with engineering only — we can do 30 minutes Mon afternoon.

-Aditya
